ambiguities.text: The specification states DELEGATECALL enables 'mutable code sources' without clarifying security implications of delegation to untrusted code.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume DELEGATECALL to untrusted addresses is a security risk since the target code can arbitrarily modify caller's storage. Security depends on caller properly validating delegation targets.

ambiguities.text: The behavior when the target address has no code is not explicitly specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume DELEGATECALL to an address with no code succeeds but performs no operation, similar to CALL behavior.

implicit_assumptions.description: The caller trusts the target contract code not to maliciously modify storage or perform unauthorized actions.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Delegating to malicious code could drain funds, corrupt storage, or exploit the caller's permissions.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot force a contract to DELEGATECALL to an arbitrary address unless the contract's logic permits it.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If delegation target can be controlled by attacker, they could execute arbitrary code in victim's context.
